tier: Japan D zone private room (dedicated IPv4 and IPv6)

free_tier.stated: No free tier. Japan D zone dedicated is $29.99 a month: 1 CPU, 2048 MB RAM, 30 GB NVMe, 100 Mbps peak, 10 TB a month in plus out (throttled above), one dedicated IPv6 with all ports and one dedicated IPv4 that is fixed and does not change. The product page showed 'sold out' on 2026-11-03. Other private-room zones are C at $99.99, E at $129.99 and H at $29.99 a month.
free_tier.notes: The listing page for private rooms shows the five zone prices; the D zone page states the specification and the sold-out state.

retention.stated: not applicable: a rented machine and its address, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The page states the IPv4 and the IPv6 are fixed and do not change; an address-retention term at non-payment is not stated.

egress.terms: 10 TB a month counted as in plus out, with speed reduced above the allowance. The 100 Mbps figure is a peak: the page says the actual rate falls when the line is congested. Some high-risk IPv4 ports are blocked by the ISP, for example 25, 80 and 443.
egress.free_allowance: 10 TB per month (in plus out) on the D zone

interface_detail: A virtual dedicated server (the page says all private-room products are VDS) with a fixed IPv4 and IPv6; the access method is not stated on the product page.
tooling: An SSH or RDP client, whichever the image supports, plus a proxy or tunnel daemon the user installs on the machine. The vendor publishes no proxy endpoint on the pages read.
chaining: A Worker opens an outbound connection to the server's fixed IPv4 and the server makes the upstream request, so the upstream sees an address on the ISP line the vendor sells. Some ports, for example 25, 80 and 443, are disabled by the ISP on the IPv4 per the page.

limits.value: 10 TB per month in plus out on the D zone, speed reduced above it
100 Mbps peak on the D zone, lower when the line is congested

limits_note: Stock decides this record: the D zone was sold out when read. The vendor's own pages do not use the word residential; they say the IPv4 ports are blocked by the ISP. A third-party test report of an earlier sososo plan titles it a BIGLOBE home-broadband VPS, which is reported, not verified for this plan.
binding_note: The 10 TB allowance is far above a low-volume exit. What decides the record is stock and the unverified registration class.

identity_cost.detail: The registration form marks first name, last name, email, password and password confirmation as required (asterisks); phone, company, country, address and city are not marked required. Payment routes the notice lists are crypto through two processors, Alipay QR, Revolut and Wise (the last three confirmed by hand). Whether a card is accepted is unverified.

reliability_note: The home page carries a notice dated 2026-10-18 that the site had been upgraded and should work normally again, so the storefront had an outage that month.
confidence_note: Price, specification, stock and registration fields are documented from the vendor's shop pages. The residential label is third-party and the registration class is unverified because no test address is published.

notes: sososo sells Japanese lines on a Paymenter storefront in three groups: shared rooms (VPS), private rooms (VDS) and takeout services. This record covers the private-room D zone, the cheapest dedicated-IPv4 line; the Rakuten 5G mobile private room is its own record. Whether the D zone address is registered to a consumer ISP is unverified: the page publishes no test address.
